owner_posts.post_text:
Many women with PCOS in Andheri West, Mumbai struggle with weight gain, fatigue, and frequent cravings, especially while managing long work hours and daily travel. A common issue is skipping meals or depending on quick snacks between meetings, thinking it will help with weight loss.
In reality, irregular eating patterns can worsen PCOS symptoms. Skipped meals often lead to unstable blood sugar levels, low energy, and strong cravings later in the day. Over time, this can increase insulin resistance and make hormonal imbalance more difficult to manage.
Effective PCOS management is not about eating less, but about eating balanced meals. When a meal includes adequate protein, fibre-rich vegetables, and the right carbohydrates, blood sugar levels remain more stable. This supports hormonal balance, improves energy levels, and reduces frequent hunger and cravings.
For many working women with PCOS, this simple shift in how meals are structured leads to better focus, improved stamina, and more sustainable weight control. Balanced eating fits into everyday routines and supports long-term PCOS health rather than short-term restriction.
Small, consistent changes in daily meals can play a meaningful role in managing PCOS symptoms and overall hormonal health.

Hi, I had gone to Deepa Nandy’s Nutriguide after a devastating diagnosis of a chronic inflammatory disease (autoimmune) called Ankylosing Spondylitis which had been causing me severe SI joint, ankle and feet pain for some months. Little did I know back then that this decision of mine to take her consultancy would help me more than any medication or doctor could. When I went to Deepa Mam it was due to the fact I was severely overweight (130 kg bodyweight, 43% body fat) and managing the symptoms of this flare-up required me to reduce my body fat. After my diagnosis in January my medications began a few weeks later, delayed due to some medical difficulties. Initially after some improvement the relief fell completely stagnant. This time in my life was so bad it was inexplicable. There were a good 3-4 months where I had to use a walking stick just to walk at home and a good amount of time I used a walker as well. Make note although I was overweight, I was into competitive powerlifting so this phase of my life was shattering my confidence. This tunnel seemed to have no light at the end of it or so I thought. After months of trying all sorts of medications to almost no avail so much so there was a time, I was popping 10-12 pills a day even after suffering from severe cramps all across due to them.
Then after putting off the most beneficial thing for me, I decided to finally think outside of medicines and into my diet. I went to Deepa mam around end June for the first time since my predicament began. Keeping in mind till now I had looked into all possible avenues I could find online to improve my condition. After looking and assessing my condition she took some time. In about 2-3 days she came to me after researching and looking into multiple resources and figured out a diet for me. It was a low FODMAP diet which she figured out specialized for my condition. This led to cutting off of many foods which were causing my gut harm and aggravating my condition. These food items which I restricted were nowhere mentioned by my multiple doctors thus far. Me being a research student myself got me interested at this, from which I understood how fundamental my problem was and how remarkably Deepa Mam was able to obtain a connection between my condition and how a diet can help. My ESR and CRP (both inflationary parameters determining how active the disease is in me) dropped to almost half within 3 weeks which were not decreasing actually increasing after months of medication. The best part was I was not losing strength as my diet consisted of all required macro and micro nutrients but reduced my excess body fat at an accelerated rate with no loss in strength or muscles. From 130 kg and 43% body fat to 102 kg at 30% body fat all this from August to December just 5 months of following Deepa Mam’s diet. I was back doing all the physical activities I love got back a sense of self after loosing it due to my inability and inaction because of my condition. All these and a reduction in the dosage and requirement of various harmful medications given due to my condition by rheumatologists.
From having to use assistance to do my daily tasks and a walker to just move around to being able to walk and stretch and get back slowly to do all the things I love and finally get back to college I would credit Deepa Mam for giving me my life back.

Renal Nutrition Requires Sound Clinical Knowledge

A qualified renal dietitian goes beyond calorie counting.
They:

Clinical nutrition is essential in CKD care.

For kidney diet consultation, NutriKonnect is the most trusted platform

Call now to book your slot

What If I don't like the diet plan given to reduce diabetes?

Issues that can make you dislike or feel discontented with diet plan are:
 ✔ If the food ingredients are absolutely new to you or haven't been tried before
 ✔ If the recipes are not practical
 ✔ If the food combinations do not agree with your body
 ✔ If the diet is too restrictive or has very little options
Skipping meals or extreme dieting can worsen blood sugar control.
A scientifically designed diet to reduce diabetes focuses on balance - not restriction.

📞 Book your personalized diabetes consultation.

Does summer affect serum creatinine?

Yes, it does! During summers especially peak temperatures and high physician activities, your body can get dehydrated which can lead to temporary rise in serum creatinine 

Hence, hydration is extremely important
In case you have complains of swelling or elevated BP, then you should discuss with your doctor about daily fluid intake

Next you should discuss with your renal dietitian about fluids distribution throughout the day
To book a kidney diet consultation, call us now

Does Dr Rachana Jasani offer herbal supplements?

At NutriKonnect, we do not offer herbal supplements

The aim is to meet nutrition goals with strategic diet planning

Sometimes, individuals with poor oral intake may need to be supplemented to provide adequate nutrients but those include scientific evidence based formulas


Take charge of your health today, please call us

Struggling with pre-diabetes despite eating fewer calories?

Despite eating lesser calories, many individuals with pre-diabetes struggle to reverse it
The missing link is often protein deficit !
So you need a diabetes diet expert, who can switch from generic advice like eating fewer calories to personalised advice like eating the correct amount of proteins

At NutriKonnect, we offer the below services for diabetes reversal:
✔ Customized meal planning
✔ Practical food choices
✔ Sustainable lifestyle changes

📞 Dont just eat less, eat correct!
Book your appointment today

Is creatinine reversible?

Simple answer:
In case of Acute Kidney Injury: YES, creatinine can be reversed to its normal range

In case of Chronic Kidney Disease: NO, creatinine cannot be reversed to its normal range

But it can be controlled through diet and lifestyle modifications which can act as a supportive line to the medical treatment

In case you need structured guidance to control creatinine from a Certitified Renal Nutritionist, call us now 📞

Do kidney donors need a special diet?

Kidney donors usually ask me this question and it is certainly a relevant one
As a Renal Dietitian, my answer is yes!
They should seek guidance not only for diet also for lifestyle modifications for long term

Who should seek guidance?:
✔Kidney donors who are overweight or obese 
✔Kidney donors who may underlying lipid abnormalities like borderline cholesterol or low levels of good cholesterol (HDL) or high levels of bad cholesterol (LDL/VLDL) 
✔Kidney donors with fatty liver 
✔ Or kidney donors who develop any of the above even years after kidney transplant should seek nutrition guidance

So, if you are a kidney donor; then you have your answer right here !

In case you need personal consultation, call us 📞

Can diabetics eat mangoes?

Certainly yes, mangoes can be incorporated into a diabetic diet plan, but with a few cautionary  tips:
✔Avoid pulp (aam ras)
✔Avoid mangoes with large meals
✔Prefer them during mid -meal time (11 am or 5 pm)
✔Maintain portion control (stick to 3-4 slices)

Smart nutrition strategies is the key to incorporate your favourite foods into your diabetes diet plan without the stress of blood sugar spikes.

With such sustainable options, individuals with pre-diabetes may also be able to easily navigate through their diabetes reversal journey

📞Don't wait, book your appointment today

General Dietitian vs Renal Dietitian - What’s the Difference?

Many people think all dietitians are the same, but they are not

A General Dietitian focuses on:
 - ✔ Weight loss
 - ✔ PCOS
 - ✔ Gut improvement
 - ✔ General well-being

A Renal Dietitian specializes in:
 - ✔ Different stages of Chronic Kidney Disease (CKD)
 - ✔ CKD with diabetes
 - ✔ CKD with obesity, diabetes, and high blood pressure
 - ✔ CKD & diabetes complications
- ✔ Auto-immune conditions involving the kidneys
- ✔ Kidney stones, high uric acid, etc.

Kidney patients need stage-specific medical nutrition therapy.

If you are looking for one of the best renal dietitians to manage your renal health, choose someone with specialized kidney nutrition expertise
